key_insight: Deep sequence models are more robust than tabular baselines for PV forecasting when NWP inputs are realistically perturbed, because they better filter temporally correlated noise and shift reliance to stable historical/physical signals.
engineering_relevance: For operational PV forecasting, robustness under forecast uncertainty should be treated as a first-class selection criterion alongside accuracy and latency.
method: Physically constrained simulation with virtual PV power to isolate input-error propagation
Dynamic NWP perturbations with clear-sky-modulated heteroscedasticity and radiation-consistent Erbs reconstruction
Model comparison using SHAP and Integrated Gradients plus Pareto analysis of accuracy, robustness, and latency
evidence_signal: Six models, including PatchTST, GRU, N-HITS, and LightGBM, were evaluated under dynamic NWP error scenarios rather than perfect-forecast assumptions.
watch_item: Results come from a controlled virtual-PV framework, so site-specific plant effects and real operational edge cases still need validation before deployment.
paper_title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
